note: The lineage runs 3B to 200B in four stages. The 40B the assignment names is stage three, not the start: it is grown from a trained 8B, which was grown from a trained 3B. The method is the four-stage state-preserving growth of arXiv:2606.07404, this project's own prior work, which grew one lineage from a small dense seed through 5B and 9B mixtures of experts to a 120B model. Sizes below are the plan; the corpus figures are what this project is responsible for, and the 40B's is the only one derived rather than proposed.

method.source: arXiv:2606.07404, Reversible Foundations: Training a 120B Sparse MoE through State-Preserving Scaling
method.principle: Each larger model is grown from the trained weights of the smaller one rather than trained afresh.

axes.what: One feed-forward block becomes many, and a router learns to send each token to a few of them.
axes.why_it_matters_for_data: Capacity rises without a matching rise in compute per token, so the corpus does not have to grow in step with the parameter count.

axes.what: Layers are added to a trained stack rather than a deeper stack being trained from scratch.
axes.why_it_matters_for_data: The tokens already read are inherited. Depth added late does not re-read the corpus, which is why the seed's data quality outlives the seed.

axes.what: The expert count rises — in the reported lineage, to 460 under top-12 routing.
axes.why_it_matters_for_data: More experts specialise only if the mixture gives them something to specialise on. A corpus that is 90% English web text produces experts that all learn English web text.

method.warning: The paper reports that several of the failures from getting an expansion wrong are silent — the model trains, the loss falls, and the capability is simply absent. That is the same failure mode this project's five data invariants exist to catch, one level down the stack.

stages.name: The seed
stages.corpus_basis: About a trillion tokens per billion parameters, which is where Gemma 3's own family sits at this size — its 4B took 4T.
stages.asks_of_the_corpus: Everything, and it is the only stage this catalogue can actually supply. 3T asks for 60B unique tokens of natural Indian-language text and 84.9B can be committed today. Every token read here is inherited by all three stages above, so this is where provenance, licensing and decontamination have to be right rather than fixed later — and the one stage where getting it right is affordable.

stages.name: Grow it
stages.corpus_basis: Same family slope. Gemma 3's 12B took 12T and Llama 3.1's 8B took 15T, so 8T is conservative for this size.
stages.asks_of_the_corpus: The first stage the Indic pool cannot fill: 160B unique needed against 84.9B committable, short by nearly half. Everything else at this size is abundant, which is exactly what makes the shortfall specific rather than general.

stages.name: The assignment
stages.corpus_basis: Gemma-4 class, and the only corpus figure here that is derived: Gemma 3's officially stated 14T for the 27B, plus 20% for one generation. Gemma 4 discloses no token count of its own.
stages.asks_of_the_corpus: 336B unique natural Indian tokens, four times what the catalogue can commit. This is the model the whole page is about, and it is the stage where the Indic gap stops being a rounding error and becomes the plan's binding constraint.

stages.name: Frontier parity
stages.corpus_basis: Frontier scale: Llama 4 trained on over 30T and Qwen3 on 36T across 119 languages. 30T is parity, not ambition.
stages.asks_of_the_corpus: 600B unique natural Indian tokens — seven times what exists in the catalogue — and the step where the architecture changes. Going sparse buys capacity at roughly a tenth of the compute per token, which is what makes 200B affordable at all; it does nothing whatever for the Indian-language supply.

config.web_data: full corpus, plus the hardest subsets

acquisition_strategy.rule: Create or partner. Do not purchase.
acquisition_strategy.detail: The corpus is assembled from open sources, from data this project generates itself, and from partnerships and grants — not from bought licences. That is a constraint on the plan rather than a preference, and it changes which blocked datasets are worth pursuing: a letter to a ministry and a data-sharing MoU are in scope, and a commercial publisher licence is not.
acquisition_strategy.consequence: It also raises the value of the three zero-cost items in the acquisition register above everything else in it, and makes the licence questions in the catalogue the highest-leverage unresolved work in the whole project — because an answered licence costs nothing and a bought one is off the table.

invariant.claim: The natural Indian-language pool is a fixed quantity. Holding its share constant means needing more of it at every stage, and there is no more of it.
invariant.detail: The mixture reserves 8% of every batch for natural Indian-language text, read four times. At the 3B seed that asks for 60B unique tokens; at 8B, 160B; at 40B, 336B; at 200B, 600B. What this catalogue can commit is 84.9B of verified human-origin text. It covers the first stage and nothing above it.
invariant.consequence: Every stage of growth makes the Indic tier harder to fill, not easier. The only remedies are collection and partnership, and both are decisions taken years before the model trains.

gap.note: Measured against the seed. This is the finding the exercise exists to produce, and it is the opposite of what most readers expect.
gap.surprise: Every tier is short, and the two that are shortest are the ones nobody expects. Natural Indian text is covered at 25% once machine translation is excluded from the count. Indian civilizational literature is covered at 0% because not one of the 145 catalogued datasets supplies it. What is missing elsewhere — general web, code, maths — is abundant and blocked on a licence nobody has established.
gap.reading: A reader arrives assuming an India-first corpus fails on Indian data. It does not. It fails on the ordinary bulk that everybody assumes is free, and it fails for legal reasons rather than technical ones.

indic_supply.note: The Indic supply route the action chapter kept missing. Every dataset here is already open — its licence permits commercial use — and every one is blocked on work nobody has done rather than on anyone's permission. That distinction is why they never appeared in a queue built around letters.
indic_supply.source: docs/ATLAS.md sections on speech and the week 4-8 plan

asr_route.claim: ASR transcription is one of the only ways to manufacture genuinely natural Indic text at scale.
asr_route.why: India is an oral-first information economy: enormous amounts of Indic language were never written down, so they cannot be crawled. Transcription is the only way to reach them.

hours.source: docs/ATLAS.md — open, permissively-licensed Indic speech across IndicVoices, Vaani, SPRING-INX, Shrutilipi, Kathbath and SYSPIN

asr_route.caveat: Small in raw token terms and extraordinary in distributional value: it is the conversational register web text completely lacks, and conversation is this model's stated primary task. No token figure is given here on purpose — the Atlas counts words, the conversion depends on a tokenizer nobody has trained, and counting it is the first task rather than an assumption.

shape.note: What actually grows, across the lineage, and what does not.
shape.finding: Parameters rise sixty-seven fold and the corpus tenfold, while the natural Indian-language text anybody can commit does not move at all. The 3B seed is the only stage its supply covers; by the 40B it is four times short and by 200B seven. Growth does not dilute the Indic share on the chart — the mixture reserves 8% at every stage — it makes that 8% progressively impossible to fill.

config_note:
What a data plan actually decides, stage by stage. Parameter counts belong to whoever designs the architecture; sequence length, what data is admitted and when the quarantine lifts are the corpus team's decisions, and they are the ones that change what has to be collected.

Every stage runs its own complete learning-rate cycle rather than one schedule across the lineage, because each stage is a larger model than the last and reaches a different loss.

Sequence length holds at 8,192 from stage two on. Extending context is an annealing phase after pre-training rather than a stage of it, and no figure for it is proposed here because nothing in this project has measured what it would cost.

quarantine.rule: Script quarantine is absolute at the seed and enforced everywhere above it.
quarantine.what: No code-mixed or romanised Indic text in pre-training. Hinglish and Tanglish enter at instruction tuning, not before.
quarantine.why: A recurrence model accumulates state across a sequence, so a stray Latin token inside a Brahmic one corrupts the state for everything after it. On this architecture mixed script is a structural fault rather than a quality preference — which is a claim from the reference design and is recorded as one, not as a measurement.
quarantine.consequence: It is also the rule that makes the seed stage so hard to fill: the cleanest Indic text is the scarcest, and quarantine removes the code-mixed material that would otherwise pad it.
